title: The map
logline: A perfect map of Small Wood in ninety seconds. Accurate in 1997.

panels.composition: The Driftwood Motel night-audit desk, 2:10 AM. A CRT, a bell, a key rack. WOOD in a motel polo drawing on the back of a registration card. Down the hall, the ice machine — its hum drawn as a low flat line under the panel.

characters.pose: at the desk in a polo, drawing on a card

image.prompt: a lean man in a motel polo shirt drawing on the back of a card at a night-audit desk with a CRT and a bell, key rack behind, a dim hallway with an ice machine, razor-sharp brush and ink, clean architectural perspective

panels.composition: A GUEST in a bathrobe at the counter.

characters.pose: in a bathrobe, hair flat on one side

balloons.text: Do you have a map of the town?

image.prompt: a man in a white bathrobe with hair flat on one side leaning on a motel front desk at night, a clerk not yet looking up

panels.composition: Wood slides the registration card across: on the back, a perfect ink map of Small Wood, every building, drawn in the ninety seconds since panel 1.
props: the card with an intricate ink map

image.prompt: close-up of a hand sliding a small card across a desk, on its back an intricate perfect ink map of a small coastal town with every building drawn
image.notes: The map should read as astonishingly detailed for its size.

panels.composition: The guest holds the card up.

characters.pose: holding the card up to the light

image.prompt: a man in a bathrobe holding a small card up to the light at a motel desk while the clerk goes back to drawing, a hallway ice machine in the background

notes: The ice machine's hum line runs under all four panels — the substrate's pitch, if the reader of vol 6 wants it; a motel noise otherwise.
